children: The dollar will likely trade between 4.03 ringgit and 4.06 ringgit next week, with investors likely to remain cautious ahead of U.S. inflation data, Kenanga economists say in a note. An in-line CPI reading would open a retest of 4.030, while evidence of broadening services inflation could push the dollar toward 4.060 ringgit, they reckon. The Fed is expected to stand pat in September, with the first rate cut in 2Q, while Warsh's speech could be a test rather than policy signal, they say. Markets will also monitor U.S.-Iran developments and oil prices, with the ECB's expected 25bp hike likely to have limited spillover on the ringgit, they add. Kenanga expects the dollar to face resistance at 4.049 ringgit, with support at 4.030 ringgit. The dollar is flat at 4.0441 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
